claims.text: Microsoft’s Recall feature became a privacy scandal in 2024 because, despite claims that data was encrypted, security researchers demonstrated that screenshots were stored unencrypted (in plaintext) in a local SQLite database [Source: ev-1].
This meant sensitive information visible on the screen—such as passwords and private messages—was captured by default and accessible to any process running under the user's account [Source: ev-1].
The feature had been announced on May 20, 2024, at Microsoft Build as an AI "memory" tool that took frequent screenshots of the user's screen [Source: ev-1].

In response to the controversy and inquiries from regulators such as the Irish Data Protection Commission, the UK Information Commissioner’s Office, and the Washington State Attorney General, Microsoft delayed the release in June 2024 and fundamentally changed its design [Source: ev-1].
The relaunched version is now opt-in (default OFF), requires Windows Hello authentication and presence detection to access the timeline, and excludes incognito or DRM content [Source: ev-1].
This revised, privacy-focused version reached general availability on Copilot+ PCs in 2025 [Source: ev-1].
